_readme: PORTED to the method-template format read by replay_holograms.py. This reproduces the July 2026 run (replay_simulation_20260724_174615) exactly: same four methods, same 750-iteration sources under GD+CITL/simulations, same two conditions, same 18 targets, 144 captures. Nothing about which hologram is displayed has changed; only the way the source is expressed moved from a hardcoded METHOD_SOURCES dict in the script into this file. The original run directory holds its own copy of the pre-port config, so provenance for the published captures is preserved there regardless of this file. allow_newest is deliberately absent everywhere: the original raised on more than one match and that strictness is worth keeping for a run whose numbers are already in a manuscript.

experiment.description: Experimental capture of simulation-generated holograms (GS, GD, per-target transformer, batched transformer) under both physics conditions, at the published 750-iteration operating point. Replay only, no training, no camera-in-the-loop.

run._comment: 750 iterations matches the count used by GD+CITL, SAIL and batched SAIL on the bench, so the experimental columns are on equal footing. The published simulation table quotes 1500 for GS/GD separately; that is a different comparison and not what this capture is for. Capture keys are decoupled from on-disk folders: transformer_per_target reads outputs/transformer/ (per-target model, written by evaluate_transformer_once) and transformer_batched reads the batched 18-target model. These replaced the older opaque transformer/shared_model pair, which said nothing about the training regime.

hardware._comment: Identical to sail.json / camera_feedback_gs_gd.json / batched_sail.json. The rig is locked and calibrated; these values must not diverge from the CITL runs or the captures stop being comparable. dll_path is a LIST: the original hardcoded one user's path and would not have loaded the EDSDK on the other machine.
